name: CI

# The PR gate: build, typecheck, test, lint, and the publish/provenance checks — everything `ready`
# plus the gates covers, split into parallel jobs. Runs on every PR and on pushes to main so a
# regression is caught before merge, not at docs-deploy or release-tag time.

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # `workflow_dispatch` lets CodSpeed trigger a backtest run to seed baseline data for the
  # `benchmarks` job; jobs gated on `pull_request` simply no-op on a manual run.
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

# Supersede in-flight PR runs; let main runs finish.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# Every job carries `timeout-minutes`. release.yml's gate waits on this workflow's conclusion with a
# 1-hour deadline, so a job left on the 6-hour default can hang the release even when it's advisory.
# Values are ~2.5x observed runtime — these catch hangs, not slow-but-working jobs.

env:
  # vp's task cache stores task OUTPUTS as .tar.zst tarballs, so a cache hit re-materializes the
  # gitignored generated dirs. The `build` job warms it; downstream jobs restore and replay the
  # recursive build. Keep that build serial: concurrent output replay can remove a workspace
  # dependency while another package's generator imports it.
  #
  # Key shape: `<prefix><os>-<hash(pnpm-lock.yaml, vite.config.ts)>-<run_id>-<run_attempt>`.
  #
  # The hash segment has to be in the SAVE key, not just the restore-keys — a restore-key only ever
  # matches a key some run actually wrote. Omitting it made `<prefix><os>-<hash>-` dead config that
  # could never match, silently degrading every restore to the broad `<prefix><os>-` fallback (i.e.
  # "the newest cache from any lockfile").
  #
  # The run_id/run_attempt tail keeps each attempt's key unique, because GH Actions cache keys are
  # immutable: a sha-based key can never be resaved by a rerun, so a `build` job whose auto-tracked
  # output snapshot was incomplete for that attempt would pin every downstream job (and every rerun of
  # the same commit) to that broken tarball forever. A fresh key per attempt means a rerun always
  # saves, and downstream jobs in this attempt exact-match this attempt's own build.
  VP_TASK_CACHE: node_modules/.vite/task-cache
  VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX: vp-taskcache-

jobs:
  automation-guard:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/guard-release-automation.yml
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@3754dd7dbdb32bd8f6d28b6043de13ad3a75f21f # v1.21.1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore/save vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Build all packages
        run: vp run -r --concurrency-limit 1 build
        env:
          CODECOV_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}

  component-accessibility:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 120
    continue-on-error: true
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@3754dd7dbdb32bd8f6d28b6043de13ad3a75f21f # v1.21.1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r --concurrency-limit 1 build
      - name: Re-audit components whose inputs changed
        id: audit
        run: vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:accessibility
      - name: Require committed evidence to match
        id: evidence
        run: git diff --exit-code -- docs/public/accessibility/results.json
      - name: Summarize advisory results
        if: always()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          found=false
          for summary in a11y-report/*/index.md; do
            if [ -f "$summary" ]; then
              cat "$summary" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
              found=true
            fi
          done
          if [ "${{ steps.audit.outcome }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "The accessibility audit did not complete successfully; this is not a clean audit." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          elif [ "${{ steps.evidence.outcome }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Committed accessibility evidence is stale; this is not a clean audit." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          elif [ "$found" = false ]; then
            echo "Accessibility evidence is current; no component needed re-auditing." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
      - name: Upload advisory accessibility evidence
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7
        with:
          name: component-accessibility
          path: a11y-report/
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

  typecheck:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up Vite+
        uses: voidzero-dev/setup-vp@3754dd7dbdb32bd8f6d28b6043de13ad3a75f21f # v1.21.1
        with:
          cache: true
          run-install: true
      - name: Restore vp task cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ${{ env.VP_TASK_CACHE }}
          key: ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pnpm-lock.yaml', 'vite.config.ts') }}-
            ${{ env.VP_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX }}${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Materialize generated output
        run: vp run -r --concurrency-limit 1 build
      - name: Generate docs theme curve
        run: node docs/scripts/site-themes.ts
      - name: Typecheck
        run: vp check

  foundation_changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      foundation: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.foundation }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Detect Foundation support changes
        id: filter
        uses: dorny/paths-filter@ceb8a2b8f2d89434be7ff52d3de7ec3738c5cc9d # v4.0.3
        with:
          filters: |
            foundation:
              - 'renderers/foundation/**'
              - 'scripts/quality/with-target-version.ts'
              - 'scripts/release/target-compatibility.json'
              - 'formats/tokens/**'
              - 'formats/components/**'

# Build, release, and the docs site

## Generated values and translation identity

Compatibility Markdown is formatted through `vite-plus/fmt` before it is written, so running
`sync:compatibility` doesn't need a later table-format repair commit.

Generated package compatibility paragraphs opt in with `<!-- pantoken-generated-values -->`.
Their code spans and link destinations become stable `{{ptk_code_N}}` placeholders during
extraction and lookup. Generated JS callouts use the same contract; authored descriptions,
examples, and prose numbers don't opt in automatically. CSS value/code columns and HTML `<code>`
content already stay outside translatable units.

The compatibility page opts in at whole-file level. Its generated tables normalize padding before
keying, and the **Current format** column treats numeric version metadata as bindings while keeping
its explanatory words translatable. Status, limitations, reasons, new rows, and grammatical changes
still need translations. Generated API templates include a stable page scope so existing translations
with different wording aren't merged just because their machine values differ.

After generating English API pages, migrate existing catalogs without invoking a provider:

```sh
vp exec node scripts/release/migrate-generated-values.ts --check
vp exec node scripts/release/migrate-generated-values.ts --write
vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:values:render
vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:values:check
```

Migration preserves unrelated catalog formatting, headers, comments, and obsolete history.
An obsolete, non-fuzzy translation can seed a new active generated entry only when its literal
English source exactly matches the current generated source; the historical entry stays unchanged.
It preserves fuzzy/empty entries as incomplete and rejects conflicting or ambiguous mappings.
Review those entries separately; don't clear their flags just to pass the gate.
The renderer also refuses incomplete generated templates. These commands never start an AI adapter.
The normal API locale build refreshes compatibility guide values before rendering package pages.

The guide translation command retries nonempty fuzzy generated templates through the configured
provider. It validates restored placeholders before saving a response or clearing fuzzy flags.
Failed translations remain incomplete and aren't rendered as reviewed compatibility pages.

Bindings are restored from each current source after translation lookup. A template can outlive a
version bump without retaining the old value. Missing, repeated, unknown, or corrupted slots fail;
they never silently fall back to stale data. Rendered Markdown, HTML, and agent-facing exports
contain literal values, not unresolved placeholders.

## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly

- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
  [-F <glob>] <bin>`.
- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns core CSS
  correctness; cssdoc owns documentation comments. `lint:css` and `lint:cssdoc` run in `ready`, and
  both are wired into the `vite.config.ts` staged hook.

`vpr docs:dev` builds interactions before staging its browser bundles. The interactions build task
declares its workspace dependencies' builds as prerequisites, so `@pantoken/utils` is built even
when its `dist` output is missing. Run `vp run @pantoken/interactions#build` rather than invoking
`scripts/build-iife.ts` directly when prerequisites haven't been built.
CSS generation also declares both runtime and development workspace builds as prerequisites:
its generator imports `@pantoken/plugin-props-minify` from development dependencies. Keep these
prerequisites on the generator task so standalone generation and docs startup use the same order.

## Accessibility evidence in the docs build

The docs build keeps the checked-in evidence (`docs/public/accessibility/results.json`) current, so
the `## Accessibility` tables on each CSS API page match the code that ships. The `accessibility`
asset task (`docs/scripts/accessibility-refresh.ts`, run by `docs:assets`) fingerprints every audited
record from its CSS and examples, built stylesheet and behavior script, and the inputs every page
shares (tokens, base, focus, elevation, the automatica11y version, and the audit harness). It
re-audits only records whose fingerprint differs from the one stored in the snapshot and merges the
results back, so an unchanged tree is a fast no-op.

- `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:accessibility` refreshes stale records. `--check` (via
  `docs:accessibility:check`) reports them without auditing; `--all` re-audits everything; `--adopt`
  stamps current fingerprints onto existing evidence when you know the inputs didn't change the results.
- Commit the updated snapshot with the change that caused it. The `component-accessibility` CI job
  re-audits stale records and fails when the committed snapshot differs.
- On CI (or with `DOCS_ACCESSIBILITY_INSTALL_BROWSER=1`) the refresh provisions the audit browser
  when it needs one. `docs:dev` sets `DOCS_ACCESSIBILITY_AUDIT=skip` so a dev server never starts an audit.
- The tables are raw HTML in the generated page. The segmenter classifies them as `audit` blocks, so
  their visible text (headings, pill labels, details) enters `l10n/docs.api.pot` through the normal API
  translation pipeline while markup and `<code>` selectors stay verbatim. The fixed labels live in
  `ACCESSIBILITY_AUDIT_STRINGS` in `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.

## Local component accessibility reports

`vp run audit:components` is an explicit, uncached full audit task, separate from `ready` (the docs build re-audits only stale records; see above). It uses the
catalog-backed automatica11y development dependency, current local package builds, and authored
component examples. It doesn't send examples to a remote audit service.
The task first runs the shared `build:all` prerequisite, restoring the complete workspace build
graph in dependency order. A fresh checkout or restored CI task cache doesn't contain package
outputs until those tasks run; building only components, CSS, and interactions can leave their
build-time workspace dependencies missing.

The tool requires Chrome or Chromium. Check setup with
`vp exec -F @pantoken/components automatica11y doctor`. If a browser is missing, explicitly opt into
its download with `vp exec -F @pantoken/components automatica11y doctor --install-browser`.
Don't bypass an outdated-browser warning without understanding its effect on results.

Each run retains the tool's original Markdown and JSON reports and a coverage index in
`a11y-report/<run>/`. The command returns an error for infrastructure failures; accessibility
violations alone don't fail it. Keep axe and IBM findings separate, and read incomplete and
needs-review results rather than treating an empty violations list as a verdict.
The index separates explicit gaps/undetermined checks from coverage notices and lists tier
execution per target, archetype, and state. Notices preserve `outcome.coverage`, summary gaps,
and not-testable notes, with missing requested tiers derived when absent from the tool's outcome.
Notices can overlap explicit gap counts; they aren't unique defects, and the counts aren't additive.
Target completion doesn't mean every requested tier ran in every state. In automatica11y 0.11.0,
